SAS NOTUPPER(string <, start>)

Source: R/doc_functions.R
sas_f_notupper.Rd

Position of the first character that is not uppercase. See the SAS documentation (Functions and CALL Routines).

Arguments

x

Character string to search. A numeric value is first converted to character with the BEST12. format.

start

Optional numeric start position, default 1. A positive value searches rightwards from that position; a negative value searches leftwards (towards the beginning) from position |start|, starting at the end of the string if |start| exceeds the length. 0, or a positive start beyond the end of the string, gives 0.

Value

A vector with one result per element (arguments are recycled), as the SAS function returns per observation.

Differences from R

SAS character values have a fixed length and are padded with blanks; trailing blanks do not count in comparisons. R strings have no fixed length.

See also

Other character functions: sas_f_anyalnum(), sas_f_anyalpha(), sas_f_anydigit(), sas_f_anylower(), sas_f_anyprint(), sas_f_anypunct(), sas_f_anyspace(), sas_f_anyupper(), sas_f_byte(), sas_f_cat(), sas_f_cats(), sas_f_catt(), sas_f_catx(), sas_f_char(), sas_f_choosec(), sas_f_coalescec(), sas_f_collate(), sas_f_compare(), sas_f_compbl(), sas_f_compress(), sas_f_count(), sas_f_countc(), sas_f_countw(), sas_f_dequote(), sas_f_find(), sas_f_findc(), sas_f_findw(), sas_f_first(), sas_f_ifc(), sas_f_index(), sas_f_indexc(), sas_f_indexw(), sas_f_klength(), sas_f_ksubstr(), sas_f_left(), sas_f_length(), sas_f_lengthc(), sas_f_lengthm(), sas_f_lengthn(), sas_f_lowcase(), sas_f_notalnum(), sas_f_notalpha(), sas_f_notdigit(), sas_f_notlower(), sas_f_notprint(), sas_f_notpunct(), sas_f_notspace(), sas_f_propcase(), sas_f_quote(), sas_f_rank(), sas_f_repeat(), sas_f_reverse(), sas_f_right(), sas_f_scan(), sas_f_strip(), sas_f_substr(), sas_f_substrn(), sas_f_translate(), sas_f_transtrn(), sas_f_tranwrd(), sas_f_trim(), sas_f_trimn(), sas_f_upcase(), sas_f_verify(), sas_f_whichc()

Examples

# NOTUPPER: each call is explained above it and followed by its result

# The first character that is not an uppercase letter is 'c' at position 3.
sas_f_notupper("ABc")  # notupper('ABc') = 3
#> [1] 3

# All characters are uppercase letters, so the result is 0.
sas_f_notupper("ABC")  # notupper('ABC') = 0
#> [1] 0

# Negative start -3 searches leftwards from position 3; the first non-uppercase
# character is 'a' at position 1.
sas_f_notupper("aBC", -3)  # notupper('aBC', -3) = 1
#> [1] 1
